title: Random subclass picks its integer generator from the nearest MRO definition of random()/getrandbits()
source: CPython commit ec1622d56c80d15740f7f8459c9a79fd55f5d3c7 (bpo-33144, GH-6563) dated 2018-05-08, fixing Lib/random.py
false_flag_note: A reviewer might flag mutating the subclass inside __init_subclass__ as surprising, or the MRO walk as over-engineered next to a simple identity check against the base class. The identity check is exactly what was wrong: it misjudged overrides inherited from an intermediate class or supplied by a mixin, installing a _randbelow that used a primitive the subclass had effectively replaced. Nearest-definition-wins is the ordinary subclassing contract, and a subclass that defines _randbelow itself still short-circuits the walk and keeps its own implementation.
